SANSKRIT GRAMMAR. [§ 340

with a क added to it; कौलेयकः 'a dog', pertaining
to a noble family'; कौशेयकः 'a sword', शैवेयकः 'a neck
ornament', कृत्सितातः भयः कुथयः तव जातः काशेयकः,
ग्रामेयकः, 'village-born, rustic'; नागरेयकः, &c.(8) कौशा
in the sense of 'made of'; कौशेयं 'a silken garment';-
(9) पुरुष in different senses; पौरुषेयः 'man-slaughter',
'human work', 'derived from or incidental to man,
composed or propounded by man'; and (10) to पथिन्,
आतिथि, बसति and स्वपति in the sense of 'useful in, good
for'; पथे साधु पाथेयं 'what is useful on the way', i. e.
'provisions for a journey'; आतिथिषु साधुः आतिथेयः
'attentive to guests, hospitable' वसौ साधुः वासतेयः
'hospitable':—यं राशिः; स्वपतेः गतं स्वपतेयं (धनं)
'wealth, property'; vide Kir. XIV. 8.

क)—is affixed (1) to words expressive of countries in the
sense of 'born or produced in'; मद्रक: 'born or pro-
duced in the Madra country';—(2) to पीत in the sense
of 'dyed with'; पीतकः 'dyed yellow';—(3) in the sense
of 'belonging to'; मद्रकः, स्वकः, &c.—(4) 'bought for'
पञ्चकः 'bought for five rupees';—(5) in the sense of
'acting' शीतकः 'one who is cold' i. e. 'slow in action,'
'a dilatory or lazy man;' उष्णकः 'an active man';—
(6. 7. 8.) to express pity or diminution, or depreciation-
पुत्रकः 'poor son' देवदत्तकः 'unhappy Devadatta'; ह्रस्वो
वृक्षो वृक्षकः, 'a small or stunted tree'; अश्वकः a bad
horse, a hack; शूद्रकः 'a wicked Sudra,' (9) and some-
times with no signification; अविकः i. e. अविः 'a ram'
मणिकः 'a jewel', बालकः 'a young boy'; &c

षु)—is affixed (1) to words denoting names of beasts, in
the sense of 'a collection of'; अविकुञ्जं 'a flock of sheep'

*, कुञ्जक्, युञ्जक, कुन्नी, कुणिडन्, ग्राम. &c.
